Reading structured answers quickly

So you can read it all in one go: the reader shows a few words at a time, each chunk centred on the letter your eye lands on. Long answers from a model are rarely just prose, though. They carry lists, code, tables and pictures, and each of those wants a different pace.

This page is the demo the tests drive. Press Space to start, and the reader stops at every chapter so you can see what is coming.

How prose is paced

Prose is streamed in short chunks. A chunk ends at the word limit, at the character limit, or at the end of a sentence, whichever comes first. Chunks that end a clause, end a sentence, or hold long words stay on screen a little longer.

After every stop the speed ramps up again over the next few chunks, so you never resume at full speed. Use the arrow keys to move by sentence and to change the speed.

Some words are far wider than the stage. Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis-and-its-very-long-relatives is one of them, and it still has to fit.

Lists are read item by item

A long list is streamed one item at a time with a counter, and nested items are indented by their depth.

  • Open the reader from the toolbar button, which reads your selection or else the main content of the page.
  • Hold Alt and click any block on a page to start reading from that point to the end of its container.
  • Use the context menu when you would rather keep both hands away from the keyboard for a while.
    • Speed read selection reads exactly the text you have highlighted on the page.
    • Speed read from here starts at the block you clicked and continues to the end.
  • Press Tab at any moment to switch to normal reading at your current position.

Short lists

A list whose items are all short is shown whole instead.

Code, tables and math

Code is never streamed: the reader stops, names the block and its size, and shows it in the exhibit pane. The function below is what splits a sentence into chunks, and chunkWords is its main limit.

export function chunkSentence(sentence: Sentence, opts: ChunkOptions): Chunk[] {
  const groups: Token[][] = [];
  let current: Token[] = [];
  let chars = 0;

  const flush = () => {
    if (current.length > 0) groups.push(current);
    current = [];
    chars = 0;
  };

  for (const token of sentence.tokens) {
    const length = token.text.length + (current.length > 0 ? 1 : 0);
    if (current.length >= opts.chunkWords || chars + length > opts.chunkChars) flush();
    current.push(token);
    chars += token.text.length + (current.length > 1 ? 1 : 0);
    if (current.length >= 2 && endsClause(token)) flush();
  }
  flush();

  // The last chunk of a sentence is shown longer.
  return groups.map((tokens, i) => ({ tokens, endsSentence: i === groups.length - 1 }));
}
export default chunkSentence;

Pictures and diagrams

Images and diagrams are shown in the exhibit pane for a few seconds, then playback continues on its own.
